title: The Chai Stall Caper
subtitle: Databases vs spreadsheets — which is right for the job?
conceptSummary: Spreadsheets are great for small data and quick math. Databases handle millions of rows, multiple tables, and complex queries.

dialogue.text: Quick break! Our informant at the chai stall has a question. He has customer data — should he use Excel or a database?
Depends on the size and complexity. This is a FUNDAMENTAL question every data detective must know.
Let me match each scenario to the right tool.

teachMoment.title: Spreadsheet vs Database
teachMoment.body:
Use a SPREADSHEET when:
• Data fits in one sheet
• You need quick calculations or charts
• Team is small, non-technical

Use a DATABASE when:
• Data has multiple related tables
• Millions of rows
• Multiple users need to read/write at once
• You need complex filtering and joining

task.instruction: Match each scenario to the best tool: Spreadsheet or Database.

matchingPairs.scenario: Tracking 50 students' grades for a semester
Managing orders for 10,000 customers across 5 cities
Hospital records for 500 doctors and 50,000 patients
Quick chart of this week's chai stall sales
E-commerce app with real-time inventory updates

hints.text: If the data is small and lives in one place, a spreadsheet works. Big, complex, or shared? Database.
Think: would you want to scroll through a million rows in Excel? That's when a database wins.

winDialogue.text: Perfect score! The chai stall uncle is impressed. He's going to start learning SQL next week!
Speaking of databases — our informant just sent a tip. There's a hidden table in the pizza database.

storyBeat: The informant reveals a secret: beyond the standard tables, there's a hidden `admin_logs` table tracking who modified the data. The SHADOW42 villain left digital footprints.
